newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuador says ready to give asylum to Peru rebels.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador says ready to give asylum to Peru rebels.

text.p: Ecuadoran President Abdala Bucaram said on Thursday he was ready to grant asylum to Peruvian rebels holding almost 400 hostages at the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima.

"We have stated clearly that if we can be of help, providing the Peruvian government asks for it, we would accede to that," Bucaram replied when asked by journalists whether Ecuador would give asylum to the Peruvian guerrillas.
Nevertheless, Bucaram said the asylum would no be political. "We cannot talk about political asylum when we see terrorism and political delinquency...in any case that expression is misused," he said.
Bucaram did not elaborate, and it was not immediately clear what kind of asylum Ecuador would grant the rebels.
The heavily-armed Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) guerrillas captured the ambassador's residence on Tuesday, taking hostage some 400 people who were attending a cocktail party.

The rebels have threatened to kill their captives, including many high-ranking diplomats, businessmen and government officials, if the Peruvian government does not release up to 500 of their jailed comrades.
